Hi Samir — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery call:

1) Primary goal: run a long-context evaluation against your 50–100k customer support threads to validate summarization fidelity and truncation behavior.
2) Key constraints: must preserve PII redaction (you mentioned SOC 2 requirements), 95th-percentile latency < 700ms for 2k-8k active users, and cost target aligned to your monthly budget threshold.
3) What we proposed on the call: a short pilot (2–3 weeks) where we run your eval harness against two model variants and a chunking + summarization baseline. We'll provide benchmark CSV, the prompt set we discussed, and a sandbox API key for the hosted long-context endpoint.

Attached: prompt-set-v1.md (initial prompt templates) and the benchmark CSV stub.

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple clarifying Qs before we hand the data to you:

1) Truncation behavior: if a thread is >64k tokens, does Redwood automatically chunk and stitch, or will tokens be dropped? We care about information loss in the lead paragraph and timeline.
2) Summarization fidelity: do you run abstractive summarization on the whole thread or extractive-first-then-abstractive? We want consistent meeting notes-level fidelity and low hallucination.
3) Security/PII: Tom is our security lead; he needs to review the SOC 2 evidence and controls before we share exports.

Also, can you share the prompt set and the exact models you’ll run so our engineering team can sanity-check?

—Samir

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Long-context evals / model recommendations

Samir — great questions. Answers below and a few concrete recommendations. (Pasting the prompt set link and benchmark summary at the bottom.)

1) Truncation / chunking behavior:
- For threads under 64k tokens we run on the single-pass long-context engine (redwood-extended-70b-64k). Tokens are not silently dropped — we use a KV cache + segmented attention kernels to preserve full context up to the model window.
- For inputs that exceed the longest-supported window (rare for your dataset), our default is to run deterministic chunking with overlap (configurable, default 256-token overlap) and an ordered-stitch stage that produces an intermediate extractive summary per chunk followed by an abstractive merge. That gives the best balance of fidelity vs. throughput.

2) Summarization fidelity / hallucinations:
- We recommend the two-model approach for the pilot:
  * redwood-extended-70b-64k (primary long-context model) — high-fidelity abstractive summarization, slightly higher cost.
  * redwood-optimized-13b-16k (baseline) — cheaper, good for extractive-first baselines and chunked workflows.
- We’ll run our regression checks (prompt-sensitivity, factuality classifiers, ROUGE-L and custom F1 on your labeled summaries). If we see regressions vs. your golden set, we’ll label and surface the failing prompts.

3) Security / PII:
- Tom — happy to loop in our Security PM for a SOC 2 evidence packet. We will only accept anonymized exports (hashing + token-level redaction) unless you request a dedicated Private deployment.

Attached and links:
- prompt-set-v1.md (attached) — initial prompt templates for thread-to-summary, timeline extraction, and ask-followups.
- acme-long-context-benchmarks.csv — sample output columns we’ll populate during the pilot (rouge_l, factuality_score, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out).
- Drive folder (shared): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF-LongContextEval
- Benchmark overview (internal): https://redwood-internal.company/benchmarks/long-context-2026

Operational notes / next steps:
- Please confirm which 1k–2k-thread sample you’re comfortable sharing (anonymized).
- We’ll provision a sandbox API key with the long-context endpoint and a small credits allotment for evaluation. Expect an email with access details within 24–48 hours after Tom signs the evidence doc.
- Proposed schedule: provision (Wed), run pilot (Thu–Mon), review results (next Tues).

If it helps, Rishi has added some technical guidance below on tokenization and recommended chunking thresholds.

Thanks — Marissa

Samir — quick technical notes from the runtime/serving side:

- Tokenization / boundary effects: long email threads often contain repeated boilerplate (signatures, disclaimers). For fidelity-critical summarization, remove or mark these sections before tokenization — we can supply a small filter script.
- Chunking thresholds: for your dataset I recommend a 32k-token single-pass target for the 64k model (leave room for prompt + generation). If you see threads >80k tokens, use the chunk+stitch pipeline with 256–512 token overlap and generate extractive anchors per chunk.
- Stitching strategy: we produce per-chunk extractive summaries, then run a second-pass abstractive merge that conditions on chunk anchors. This helps preserve timeline accuracy and reduces hallucination.
- Eval harness: we can accept your golden summaries in CSV (id, reference_summary). We’ll compute ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and a simple factuality binary classifier. We’ll also provide per-prompt failure cases so you can triage.

Operationally: if you want, we can run the pilot on a small portion of your data in the hosted sandbox. That avoids any procurement delay while Tom reviews SOC material.

—Rishi
Head of Inference Ops, Redwood Inference
